mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is held constant above 5.25% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be negative due to persistent risk aversion from higher real borrowing costs.
failure_condition: In the trigger regime, the 20-day forward return is non-negative in at least 60% of instances, or the 5-year rolling IC of FEDFUNDS vs. SPX is positive (>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in new job openings (INDPRO) signals a weakening labor market, which is associated with negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% month-over-month while INDPRO decreases by >5% month-over-month
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window in the trigger regime, the 60-day forward return is positive in more than 70% of cases, or the IC of (PAYEMS, INDPRO) vs. SPX exceeds 0.10.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) above the 12-month moving average coincides with a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return as it signals renewed consumer and builder confidence.
failure_condition: Over 48 months with HOUST in expansion, the 20-day forward return is never positive in the expansion phase, or the 5-year IC of HOUST vs. SPX is negative (< -0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 2% suggests supply-side softness, which predicts a negative S&P 500 5-day forward return.
failure_condition: During any 6-month period of INDPRO declines >2% per month, the 5-day forward return is non-negative in more than 50% of instances, or the IC is positive (>0.07).

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly rises by more than 0.3% in a month, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be negative due to immediate market repricing of inflation risk.
failure_condition: In the trigger regime, the 20-day forward return is non-negative in at least 80% of occurrences, or the 3-month IC of CPIAUCSL vs. SPX is positive (>0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment (UNRATE) and a rise in labor force participation (implied via complement proxies in this catalog) predicts a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as it signals a stronger labor market.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases by >0.2% month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: During the trigger regime, the 60-day forward return is negative in more than 70% of instances, or the IC of UNRATE vs. SPX is negative (< -0.08).

mechanism_narrative: When retail sales (implied via PAYEMS as a proxy for consumer demand) grow faster than industrial production (INDPRO) for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be positive as demand outpaces supply.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth rate > INDPRO growth rate for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In the trigger regime, the 20-day forward return is never positive, or the IC of (PAYEMS growth - INDPRO growth) vs. SPX is negative (< -0.12).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged period of declining consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% suggests disinflation, which is associated with a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as market expectations for future rate cuts improve.
failure_condition: During any 12-month disinflationary window, the 60-day forward return is negative in more than 60% of months, or the 2-year IC of CPIAUCSL vs. SPX is negative (< -0.15).
